cited.basis:
The case this tracer was built to carry. The words do not change. In the
pre-1955 witnesses they are the Oratio of the short Vespers sung after the Holy
Saturday Mass, in a service whose own rubric says the Mass has no Postcommunion
(missale-romanum-1920 41411-41413, 41564-41580; pustet-1862 36945-36948,
36993-37004). In the 1962 witness the same words stand under the heading
`Postcommunio seu Oratio` at the end of Lauds (benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962
43583-43589). A matcher keyed on (mass, proper-name) asks a pre-reform book for
a Postcommunion, gets nothing, and writes down an absence; that false absence is
already recorded in this repository at
src/sources/inventories/roman-1962-proper-translations-v1.toml and was refuted
against the page on 2026-07-31.
